properties.name: A client that meets a different build replaces the server instead of attaching and reporting
properties.rationale:
🛑 THE TESTS WERE WRITTEN AGAINST A STUB OF TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR AND OBSERVED FAILING: 3 failed, 2 passed. The two that passed are the counterweights — same build attaches, unknown attaches — which is the correct reading, because today's behaviour is right for those and wrong for the three real cases. Recorded because a failing-first test and one written after the fix both end green.

⭐ WHY THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOUR RATHER THAN REPORTING, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. The defect has been recorded six times since 2026-08-07 and every previous response improved a REPORT: `served_by.stale`, its stale_note, the AGENTS.md correction, `graph.client.json`. The skew went on happening — most expensively on 2026-08-08, when it cost a day of dogfooding and five merged PRs never ran through a live session. Five rounds of better reporting did not stop it, and that is the evidence for acting instead of announcing.

📌 AND IT REACHES A PLATFORM THE OLD DETECTION CANNOT. `exe_replaced_since_start` reads `/proc/self/exe` and tests for a ` (deleted)` suffix — Linux only. On macOS it returns `unknown`, so `served_by.stale` can never be true there, which is why nothing surfaced this to Alex at all. Comparing two independently-published `stat` results is plain POSIX and works on both.

⚠️ THE RISK ACCEPTED, STATED PLAINLY: this can stop a daemon another session is mid-write against. `--stop-shared` already accepts that risk, but with a human choosing the moment; this takes the choice automatically. It is judged the lesser harm because the alternative is a session silently writing through a surface that is not the one it was built against — which is what actually happened, six times. If it proves wrong, the mitigation is narrow: re-elect only when nothing else is attached, which the Activity tracker could answer.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether mtime is preserved by any installer path in use. reflow2's own uses `install -m 755` with no `-p`, verified today; a package manager or a `cp -p` would defeat this, and nothing checks.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Fixes `fact:the-attach-path-checks-liveness-and-identity-but-never-version` — the cause behind Alex's field report and five earlier instances since 2026-08-07.

`Rendezvous` gains `exe_fingerprint: Option<String>` — `size:mtime_nanos` of the executable, captured when the daemon starts. `ensure_server_async` now asks `should_reelect` before attaching: on a mismatch it SIGTERMs the old daemon, clears the rendezvous and elects a fresh one. On a match it attaches exactly as before.

⭐ THE COMPARAND WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT AND THE FIRST TWO CANDIDATES WERE BOTH REFUTED.
• A VERSION STRING catches nothing that matters: `Cargo.toml` read `0.42.0` all day on 2026-08-29 while a development session lost SIX cycles to stale daemons — every daemon and every client published `0.42.0`. Its coverage equals the installer fix: the upgrade path only.
• AN INODE was the second proposal and is worse: measured, `install -m 755` REWRITES IN PLACE and keeps the same inode, so it would have missed the very report that prompted the work.
• SIZE + MTIME move under BOTH — verified on both paths the same day: `install -m 755` changed size and mtime with the inode unchanged; a real `cargo build` changed inode AND mtime (4481075 -> 4488902). One `stat`, no hashing of a 326 MB binary.

⚠️ AN ABSENT FINGERPRINT MEANS REPLACE, NOT MATCH. Any daemon publishing none predates this field, so it is old by construction — and that is exactly Alex's 0.39.0 server on the first upgrade after this ships. Treating absence as agreement would have made the fix unable to fix the report that prompted it.

🛑 AND IT REFUSES TO GUESS IN TWO PLACES. If this process cannot fingerprint itself it ATTACHES rather than killing a healthy daemon on no evidence — the same refusal `served_by.stale` makes when `/proc/self/exe` is unreadable. And if the SIGTERM fails (a foreign owner, or it exited between probe and signal) it attaches anyway with a loud warning naming the manual remedy, because a session on a stale surface is degraded while a session with no design brain is stopped.
